description: issue #874, the struct-constructor twin of core-language/check/arity-procedure-declared-spelling: a `struct` type's constructor is the SECOND callable reached through the checker's exact-arity path, so it needs its own stack-neutral pin rather than inheriting the procedure one. `struct Point` called as `(pOiNt 1)` reports `Point` — the declared spelling, not the call site's and not a lowercased form. Existing struct fixtures (struct-constructor-arity-too-few/too-many) name the type `point`, where all three candidate rules coincide, so they cannot distinguish this.
